subject.title: [Bug]: Heartbeat / async system events can interrupt and effectively swallow in-progress replies in Telegram topic sessions

question: Should heartbeat and async system-event work be isolated from active Telegram topic sessions by default, or should the remaining reports be split into narrower replay, default-target, and lane-idle bugs first?
rationale: The remaining reports mix runtime scheduling, Telegram delivery boundaries, stale pending-final replay, and operator-configured heartbeat targets, so an automated fix should not choose the product boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep canonical and split after proof
options.body: Keep this issue open, collect live Telegram/current-main proof, and split confirmed remaining behaviors into narrower implementation issues or PRs.

options.title: Declare current guards sufficient
options.body: Treat the shipped active-run and pending-final guards as enough and close only if maintainers accept the later reports as fixed or separately covered.

options.title: Change heartbeat isolation policy
options.body: Move heartbeat/system-event turns into a non-preemptive isolated lane by default, accepting the need for compatibility review and upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical and split after proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, collect live Telegram/current-main proof, and split confirmed remaining behaviors into narrower implementation issues or PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main heartbeat/session guard history points here as the best available routing owner for the product-boundary decision.
